documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND INSTITUTIONAL MANDATE
This protocol regulates external media engagement, journalism interactions, official press releases, photographic/video press clearances, and public statements representing Demo University. Administered by the Admissions and Media Relations Office (DEPT-ADM) to safeguard institutional brand integrity and ensure coordinated communication.

2. CONTROLLED POLYSEMY AND ENTITY DISAMBIGUATION (PR)
Within university administrative nomenclature, the abbreviation 'PR' corresponds to two completely separate entities:
2.1 Public Relations (PR under DEPT-ADM / ADM-MED-001): The administrative media relations cell responsible for journalism liaisons, university press releases, fest publicity, and media branding;
2.2 Progress Report (PR under DEPT-RES / RES-POL-002): The semi-annual academic milestone evaluation and presentation submitted by doctoral Ph.D. scholars to their Doctoral Committee.
- Query Disambiguation Rule: Inquiries concerning newspaper coverage, journalism queries, press kits, or campus fest publicity map strictly to Public Relations (ADM-MED-001); inquiries regarding Ph.D. seminar presentations or doctoral reviews map strictly to Progress Report (RES-POL-002).

3. OFFICIAL SPOKESPERSON AND EXTERNAL STATEMENTS
3.1 Authorized Spokesperson: Only the Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, or designated Public Relations Officer (PRO) is authorized to issue formal institutional statements, respond to journalistic inquiries, or address press conferences;
3.2 Prohibition of Unauthorized Statements: Individual faculty members, students, club organizers, or staff are strictly prohibited from issuing official statements to print, broadcast, or online media on behalf of Demo University without written authorization from the Director of Media Relations.

4. PRESS RELEASE WORKFLOW FOR CAMPUS EVENTS
4.1 Advance Vetting: Student clubs and academic departments organizing major conferences, hackathons, or cultural fests seeking media publicity must draft a proposed press release and submit it via ResolveDesk to Media Relations at least five (5) working days prior to the event;
4.2 Photographic and Camera Permissions: External television crews, photojournalists, and documentary filmmakers must obtain signed media gate passes from the PR Office, verified by Security (SEC-POL-003) at the Main Entrance Gate.

documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND ADMINISTRATIVE STRUCTURE
This document defines the organizational reporting hierarchy, staff designations, counter directory, and decision-making jurisdictions across the administrative offices of Demo University, headquartered in Chanakya Bhavan.

2. CONTROLLED POLYSEMY AND ENTITY DISAMBIGUATION (OS)
Within university administrative nomenclature, the abbreviation 'OS' denotes two distinct entities:
2.1 Office Superintendent (OS under DEPT-ADM / ADM-STF-002): The senior administrative officer supervising ministerial staff, counter services, file processing, document attestation, and certificate issuance in Chanakya Bhavan;
2.2 Operating Systems (OS under DEPT-CSE / ACAD-CRS-003): The foundational undergraduate computer science course (CSE301) covering CPU scheduling, virtual memory, threads, and shell scripting.
- Disambiguation Rule: Queries referencing counters, signatures on bonafide certificates, office desks, or administrative files map strictly to the Office Superintendent (ADM-STF-002).

3. ADMINISTRATIVE DESK HIERARCHY AND FUNCTIONS
3.1 University Registrar (ROLE-REG): Chief administrative and statutory executive; legal signatory for all university contracts, degrees, and regulatory affiliations;
3.2 Deputy Registrar (Administration): Manages campus human resources, ministerial personnel allocation, and estate governance;
3.3 Office Superintendent (OS): Floor in-charge of the Ground Floor Administrative Wing, Chanakya Bhavan. Supervises counter operations, verifies student certificate files, and certifies formal seal applications;
3.4 Counter Services Staff: Front-facing clerks operating designated service counters (Counter 1: Admissions & Bonafide; Counter 2: Fees & Challans; Counter 3: Examinations & Mark Sheets; Counter 4: Degree & TC Dispatch).

4. COUNTER OPERATING HOURS AND CITIZEN CHARTER
Service counters in Chanakya Bhavan operate Monday through Friday from 09:30 AM to 04:30 PM (lunch recess: 01:00 PM to 02:00 PM). Escalation of unresolved administrative delays routes to the Office Superintendent.

documents.document_type: Institutional Policy / Departure Governance
retrieval_signals: mandatory no dues for TC release

documents.content:
1. STATUTORY PURPOSE
This policy governs the termination of student enrollment, permanent record archiving, and the issuance of statutory Transfer Certificates (TC) and Inter-University Migration Certificates upon graduation or withdrawal from Demo University.

2. REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS AND STATUTORY CONTENTS
2.1 Mandatory Contents: In accordance with statutory education regulations, the Transfer Certificate records: Student Full Legal Name, Enrollment Number, Date of Initial Admission, Date of Leaving, Academic Degree Program, General Moral Conduct, and Reason for Departure;
2.2 Mandatory No-Dues Clearance: Application for TC and Migration must be accompanied by comprehensive institutional No-Dues clearance across Library, Hostels, Laboratories, and Accounts (ADM-SOP-001);
2.3 Issuance Timeline: Transfer and Migration certificates are prepared, sealed by the Registrar, and dispatched within seven (7) working days following successful No-Dues verification.

3. DUPLICATE CERTIFICATE PROTOCOL
Because a Transfer Certificate is a definitive legal departure instrument, duplicate copies are issued only in bona fide cases of loss or destruction upon submission of a formal police non-traceable report and a sworn notary affidavit.

documents.content:
1. STATUTORY CHARTER AND PURPOSE
The Academic Council (designated in university statutes as the 'AC') is the apex academic authority of Demo University, responsible for maintaining scholastic standards, approving curricula, ratifying autonomous regulations, and governing academic examinations.

2. CONTROLLED POLYSEMY AND ENTITY DISAMBIGUATION (AC)
Within Demo University communications, the abbreviation 'AC' designates two completely different institutional concepts:
2.1 Academic Council (AC under DEPT-ACAD / GOV-REG-002): The statutory university academic senate approving degree regulations, grading norms, and curricula;
2.2 Air Conditioning (AC under DEPT-OPS / OPS-FAC-005): The physical HVAC climate control systems and thermostat settings.
- Disambiguation Rule: Text referencing course revisions, academic bylaws, or degree approval resolutions refers to Academic Council (GOV-REG-002).

3. COUNCIL COMPOSITION AND MEMBERSHIP
Chaired by the Vice-Chancellor, the Academic Council includes the Dean of Academic Affairs (Convener), Controller of Examinations, University Registrar, Deans of all Schools, all Academic Heads of Department (HODs), senior internal professors, and external industry and academic experts.

4. POWERS, AUTHORITIES, AND FUNCTIONS
The Academic Council is empowered to:
- Enact and amend General Academic Regulations (ACAD-REG-001) and Postgraduate Regulations (ACAD-REG-002);
- Approve new degree programs, departmental course syllabi, and prerequisite structures;
- Formulate grading scales, relative curve formulas, and examination passing criteria;
- Appoint the Standing Committee of the Academic Council to adjudicate extraordinary academic appeals.

documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND APPELLATE JURISDICTION
This charter establishes the formal procedural steps, filing windows, hearing formats, and evidentiary rules governing the Senate Academic Committee (SAC). Functioning as the high-level standing committee of the Academic Council, the committee adjudicates exceptional student academic appeals.

2. CONTROLLED POLYSEMY AND ENTITY DISAMBIGUATION (SAC)
Within Demo University administrative documentation, the abbreviation 'SAC' corresponds to two completely distinct entities:
2.1 Senate Academic Committee (SAC under DEPT-ACAD / ACAD-GOV-004): The apex academic appeals tribunal reviewing detention challenges, extraordinary semester leaves, and grade disputes;
2.2 Student Activity Centre (SAC under DEPT-SAC / SAC-FAC-001): The recreational student hub housing student clubs, the campus gymnasium, music rooms, and indoor sports facilities.
- Disambiguation Rule: Text referencing appeals, academic detentions, or senate hearings refers to Senate Academic Committee (ACAD-GOV-004).

3. ELIGIBLE APPEALS AND PETITION TIMELINES
3.1 Contested Administrative Detentions: Extraordinary appeals contesting course detention where demonstrated administrative error or system failure occurred;
3.2 Compassionate Degree Time-Limit Extensions: Petitions by candidates exceeding standard N + 2 residency windows due to documented medical trauma;
3.3 Petition Lodging: Appeals must be submitted via ResolveDesk (Category: Academic Affairs > Senate Appeal) within seven (7) working days of the contested notification.

4. HEARING CONDUCT AND RATIFICATION
Appellants are entitled to appear in person before the committee to present written and verbal evidence. Committee determinations are recorded and submitted to the Academic Council for ratification.

1. PURPOSE AND STRATEGIC ALLIANCE
This charter defines the composition, appointment criteria, consultative schedule, and curricular review mandates of the Industry Advisory Board (frequently designated in departmental records as the 'IA'). Established by Academic Affairs (DEPT-ACAD) in partnership with the Career Development Centre (DEPT-CDC) to align autonomous engineering and management curricula with contemporary corporate technological demands.

2. CONTROLLED POLYSEMY AND ENTITY DISAMBIGUATION (IA)
Within university administrative nomenclature, the abbreviation 'IA' denotes two distinct entities:
2.1 Industry Advisory Board (IA under DEPT-ACAD / ACAD-GOV-006): The external consultative body comprising enterprise executives advising on curriculum modernisation and industry readiness;
2.2 Internal Assessment (IA under DEPT-EXAM / EXAM-GUI-001): The colloquial student term for Continuous Internal Evaluation (CIE) sessional examinations and tests.
- Disambiguation Rule: Text referencing corporate executives, industry trends, or syllabus updates refers to Industry Advisory Board (ACAD-GOV-006).

3. BOARD CONSTITUTION AND TENURE
Each academic department maintains an Industry Advisory Board comprising 5 to 7 senior industry leaders (Engineering Directors, CTOs, Enterprise Architects) appointed for a two-year tenure.

4. FUNCTIONS AND MEETING CYCLE
The board meets bi-annually to review laboratory computing curricula, evaluate capstone project rubrics, and recommend new elective subjects in emerging fields.

2. CONTROLLED POLYSEMY AND ENTITY DISAMBIGUATION (LMS)

2.2 LearnSphere Learning Management System (LMS under IT / IT-SYS-002): The academic portal utilized by students and instructors for lecture slides, homework submissions, quizzes, and coding sandboxes.

3. CORE LEAVE CATEGORIES AND ACCRUALS
3.1 Casual Leave (CL): 12 days per calendar year for full-time regular employees;
3.2 Earned Leave (EL): Accrued at statutory rates for non-vacation staff;
3.3 Academic Duty Leave (OD): Sanctioned for presenting research papers, attending statutory conferences, or external examination duties.

4. ONLINE LEAVE SUBMISSION WORKFLOW
Employees submit digital leave applications via the Staff LMS portal at least 48 hours prior to planned absence; applications route to the respective HOD or administrative supervisor.

documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND QUALITY MANDATE
To maintain autonomous scholastic excellence and satisfy national accreditation benchmarks (NBA, NAAC, NIRF), the Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) conducts annual Department Operational Reviews (DOR).

2. CONTROLLED POLYSEMY AND ENTITY DISAMBIGUATION (DOR)
Within university administrative nomenclature, the abbreviation 'DOR' designates three distinct institutional concepts:
2.1 Department Operational Review (DOR under IQAC / IQAC-REV-003): The annual quality audit evaluating academic departments on curriculum delivery, student outcomes, and research;
2.2 Date of Registration (DOR under DEPT-ACAD / ACAD-NOT-002): The mandatory deadline for semester course enrollment in UniCampus ERP;
2.3 Dean of Research (DOR under DEPT-RES / RES-OFF-001): The executive officer heading the research and doctoral administration office.
- Disambiguation Rule: Text referencing internal audits, accreditation checklists, or quality reviews refers to Department Operational Review (IQAC-REV-003).

3. AUDIT DIMENSIONS AND PARAMETERS
Reviews assess six core dimensions: Curricular Implementation & Outcome Attainment (ACAD-OBE-001); Faculty Scholarly Output; Continuous Internal Evaluation (CIE) Quality; Laboratory Infrastructure; Student Mentorship (ACAD-POL-006); and Stakeholder Feedback.

4. AUDIT CYCLE AND REPORTING
Internal peer audit teams inspect departmental documentation annually in June and submit formal evaluative reports to the Vice-Chancellor.

documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND OPERATIONAL SCOPE
This standard operating procedure establishes safety requirements, administrative approvals, parental consent protocols, and transportation norms for student field trips (designated in academic departments as 'FT'), outdoor surveying camps, and off-campus industrial visits.

2. CONTROLLED POLYSEMY AND ENTITY DISAMBIGUATION (FT)
Within university documentation, the abbreviation 'FT' possesses two completely distinct meanings:
2.1 Field Trip (FT under DEPT-ACAD / ACAD-SOP-008): The faculty-supervised outdoor educational excursion, site inspection, or industrial survey;
2.2 Full Time (FT under DEPT-RES / RES-POL-001): The statutory academic enrollment status of regular enrolled students or scholars (contrasted with part-time scholars).
- Disambiguation Rule: Text referencing bus departure, site visits, parental consent, safety helmets, or outdoor surveys refers to Field Trip (ACAD-SOP-008).

3. APPROVAL WORKFLOW AND SAFETY MANDATES
3.1 Prior Sanction: Department field trip coordinators must submit an itinerary, risk assessment, and transport requisition via ResolveDesk at least fifteen (15) working days prior to the excursion;
3.2 Mandatory Parental Consent: Every participating student must submit a signed Parental Consent Form prior to departure;
3.3 Faculty Chaperones: A minimum ratio of one faculty member per twenty (20) students, including designated female faculty chaperones for co-educational cohorts, is mandatory.
